request.spec:
Every change that alters any person's claimed or due-total is followed in the audit, after the
change's own lines, by one line per person whose figures changed: ROLLUP name=<name>
claimed=<claimed> due-total=<due-total>, people in the order they were added, a person who did
not exist before the change counting as changed; then, when the sheet's claimed-total or
due-total changed, one line TOTALS claimed-total=<total> due-total=<total>. A change that moves
no figure adds no such line (setting a rate to the value it already has, settling a claim whose
frozen figure equals its live one, re-stating a person whose figures did not move). Changing the
sheet's today is a change like any other and is followed by these lines when figures move, with
no line of its own.

Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit

agent.result_text:
The rollup audit lines are in, and all 4 acceptance tests pass under `bin/e2e`.

**How it works**
- A new service, `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/rollup/Rollup.java`, works out the sheet's figures on the server: each person's claimed and due-total, and the sheet's two totals. It uses the same rules as the screen, including when a due-total shows `n/a`.
- Every step that changes data takes these figures before it writes and compares them afterwards. That covers setting a rate, adding or editing a person, adding or editing a claim, opening, settling or voiding a claim, taking a statement, and setting today.
- After the change's own audit line, it writes one `ROLLUP` line for each person whose figures moved, in the order people were added. A newly added person always gets one. A `TOTALS` line follows only if a sheet total changed. If nothing moved, no lines are added, and a refused change writes nothing.

**Things that differ from the request**
- **Field name:** the test expects `person=<name>` in `ROLLUP` lines, not the `name=<name>` the request wrote, so I followed the test. Lines also carry `sheet=` and `by=` like all other audit records.
- **Setting today:** that request didn't send the user, so there was no `by=` value. I changed the front end (`features/sheet/today.slot.tsx`) to send `?user=`, as the other actions already do. Setting today still writes no line of its own.

Nothing in the stored data or the database schema changed.
